p: in the sea: In a ship which was launched into the sea.
Hearken: The same doctrine of the Gospel is sown everywhere, but it it does not have the same success indeed because of the fault of man, but yet by the just judgment of God.
about him with the twelve asked: They that followed him at his heels.
without: That is to say, to strangers, and such ones as are not of us.
of this world: Which pertain to this life.
And he said unto them: Although the light of the gospel is rejected by the world, yet it ought to be lit, if for no other reason than this, that the wickedness of the world might be revealed.
And he said unto them: The more liberally that we share such gifts as God has given us with our brethren, the more bountiful God will be toward us.
And he said: The Lord sows and reaps in a manner unknown to men.
should sleep: That is, when he has finished sowing should wait both day and night not doubting that the seed should spring forth, which grows both by day and night.

knoweth not how: It is the duty of the ministers to work the ground with all diligence, and accredit the success to God: for the mighty work of the seed coming to blade and ear is mysterious, and is only known by the fruit that comes.
of herself: By a certain power which moves itself.
And he said: God uses a method that men never do, beginning with the least and ending with the greatest.
as they were able to hear: According to the ability of the hearers.
expounded all things to his disciples: Literally, "loosed", as you would say, explained to them the hard riddles.
And there arose a great storm: They that sail with Christ, although he seems to sleep ever so soundly when they are in danger, yet they are preserved by him in due time, being awakened.
Why are ye so fearful: How does it come to pass that you have no faith?
